newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Amoco, Petronas, CNPC on Kazakh Uzen shortlist.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, Petronas, CNPC on Kazakh Uzen shortlist.

text.p: Kazakhstan has shortlisted U.S. Amoco, Malaysia's Petronas and the Chinese National Petroleum Corp (CNCP) to develop its giant Uzen oil field, a Western source close to the project said on Friday.
The source said the ministry would declare a winner by the end of the month.
"We have a very aggressive schedule," he said, referring to Kazakhstan's promise to select a winner by November 1.
The source said each of the companies had placed bids in excess of $1 billion to develop the field, most likely on a production-sharing basis.
Uzen, located about 150 km (100 miles) east of the Caspian Sea in southwest Kazakhstan, has estimated recoverable reserves of up to 150 million tonnes.
It is Kazakhstan's second largest oil field after Tengiz, where Chevron and Mobil are working to tap one billion tonnes of crude.
Other bidders in the tender included Ramco of the U.K. and an alliance between Unocal of the United States and Saudi Arabia's Delta Nimir.
Kazakh state-owned Uzenmunaigaz holds the license to Uzen.

The source said it was possible the tender winner might take a stake in Uzenmunaigas, but that this was unlikely because the company has not been audited to international accounting standards, making it impossible to value.

The source said the short-list was selected on the basis of the size of their bids and that contracts would be signed by the end of the year, with definitive project agreements to follow six months later.
Shortlisted candidates are to make presentations to the Kazakh officials in mid-October.
The World Bank has estimated the total cost of rehabilating Uzen's wells to peak output at $5-$8 billion.
It approved a $109 million loan in 1995 to rehabilitate the field, where annual output fell to 2.7 million tonnes in 1995, around one-sixth of its peak level in the Soviet era.
